HOSTILE ENGAGEMENT #1.1
x PALANITE PRECINCT “FANGS OF JUSTICE”
[■] ADMINISTRATUM INCIDENT RECORD
Reference: GPD-C9/SEC/01/774.M41
Subject: Territorial dispute at Toll Crossing ███████
Opposing Party: Palanite Precinct “Fangs of Justice”
Outcome: C-9 CONTROL ESTABLISHED
Geothermal Prospect Detail C-9 entered the disputed Toll Crossing following establishment of a Palanite claim marker within the site. No record of successful negotiation has been located.
Initial contact occurred in the central workings. The western access was subsequently sealed by C-9 personnel, restricting movement through the site. At approximately the same time, Labour Assets K-117 and R-204 were reported on the eastern flank despite neither worker appearing on the initial approach record.
Both assets discharged industrial hand flamers at close range. Palanite personnel were forced from position and subsequent attempts to restore formation were disrupted by sustained las-fire from the central C-9 work party.
Heavy Labour Asset B-01 entered close contact during the resulting disorder and incapacitated an isolated Palanite from the rear. No excavation equipment was involved.
By the conclusion of the third engagement cycle, the Palanite Sergeant, Specialist and two recruits had been removed from effective action. Remaining precinct personnel withdrew from the site. Their territorial relic was subsequently reached and defiled by C-9 personnel in accordance with local challenge custom. The C-9 marker remained undisturbed.  
:: MATERIAL REVIEW ::
Post-engagement inventory identified evidence of combat stimulant use among Detail personnel. No corresponding medical issue or requisition has been located.
:: DISPOSITION ::
Territorial control: GEOTHERMAL PROSPECT DETAIL C-9
Asset acquired: TOLL CROSSING
Incident closed as local territorial enforcement matter.
No further action required.
// INCIDENT CLOSED :: POST-ENGAGEMENT PROCESSING //

engagements.report:
HOSTILE ENGAGEMENT #2.1
x VAN SAAR GANG “ETHERNETANS 2.0” 
[■] ADMINISTRATUM INCIDENT RECORD
Reference: GPD-C9/SEC/02/774.M41
Subject: Unauthorised entry into Ethernetans-controlled Mine Workings
Opposing Party: Van Saar gang “Ethernetans 2.0”
Outcome: C-9 WITHDRAWAL / OBJECTIVE INCOMPLETE
Geothermal Prospect Detail C-9 entered Mine Workings under Ethernetans control for the purpose of recovering material from secured storage caches. Initial approach followed established C-9 survey practice, with restricted labour assets advancing independently of the main work party.
The approach was disrupted by previously undocumented Van Saar detection equipment. Despite this, one C-9 element established control of the flank with support from Foreman Voss and reached one secured cache. Conflicting reports prevent identification of the individual responsible for its recovery.
The main advance was less successful. Thermal Systems Technician Ethmet Griz was caught in converging fire from multiple Ethernetans personnel and removed from effective action with critical injuries. Labour Asset R-204 was likewise incapacitated while attempting to approach from the flank. Remaining C-9 personnel reported sustained difficulty returning effective fire as casualties accumulated.
Heavy Labour Asset B-01 penetrated furthest into the defended workings and engaged Ethernetans combatant Peter Apex, identified by witnesses through the use of an articulated spider-rig. B-01 failed to incapacitate Apex during initial contact and was subsequently brought down. Foreman Voss ordered general withdrawal shortly thereafter. At this time C-9 retained one recovered cache but no longer possessed sufficient effective personnel to continue the operation without further losses.
Heavy Labour Asset B-01 remained inside the Ethernetans position.
No recovery element was assigned.  
:: DISPOSITION ::
Objective status: PARTIAL RECOVERY
Territorial control: ETHERNETANS 2.0
C-9 casualties: MULTIPLE
Critical casualty: GRIZ, Ethmet
Unrecovered personnel: HEAVY LABOUR ASSET B-01
The decision to terminate the operation while B-01 remained in hostile custody is inconsistent with prior C-9 evacuation practice.
Foreman Voss declined to amend the withdrawal order.
No explanation was entered into the incident record.
// INCIDENT CLOSED :: POST-ENGAGEMENT PROCESSING //
engagements.addenda:
[■] Post-Engagement Record
Reference: GPD-C9/POST/01/774.M41
Records attached: 03
// ATTACHMENT I //
ETHERNETANS CONTAINMENT LOG: SUBJECT B-01
Source: Ethernetans 2.0 internal security archive
Classification: Captured hostile / anomalous labour phenotype  
“Heavy Labour Asset B-01” was recovered alive following withdrawal of Geothermal Prospect Detail C-9. Subject possesses extreme physical abnormalities consistent with prolonged industrial mutation. Restraint requirements have been revised twice.
No recovery attempt has been detected.
Initial assessment considered this evidence that C-9 regarded the subject as expendable. Subsequent surveillance does not support this conclusion. Detail personnel have continued normal operations and have demonstrated accurate knowledge of Ethernetans patrol movements, firing positions and internal redeployments established after “B-01” entered custody.
Possible data breach investigated. No compromised communications, surveillance devices or unauthorised transmissions have been identified.
“B-01” has not been observed communicating with C-9.  
:: SECURITY NOTE ::
A false redeployment order was circulated exclusively among personnel assigned to the containment sector.
C-9 altered its movements accordingly.
The order was never transmitted.
[Analysis suspended pending systems audit.]
Subject status: CAPTURED
Containment status: SECURE
Information security status: UNDER REVIEW
// RECORD ENDS //
+=+=+=+=+=[ ◈ ]=+=+=+=+=+
// ATTACHMENT II //
INCIDENT REPORT: GRIZ, Ethment
Source: Hostile contact report with Van Saar gang Ethernetans 2.0
Griz sustained critical injuries during an armed confrontation with Ethernetans 2.0 personnel. C-9 workers attempted evacuation, but deteriorating conditions and continued hostile activity delayed his removal from the site.
Griz expired before transfer to external medical facilities could be completed.
Subsequent review determined that reliance on outside medical providers had resulted in unacceptable delays, excessive emergency fees and repeated demands for discretionary payments concerning the nature of C-9 personnel injuries.
Following the incident, Foreman Voss authorised the permanent attachment of a penal chirurgeon to the Detail.  
PROCUREMENT NOTE GPD-C9/SEC/01/774.M41 
External treatment estimate: 180 credits.
Recovery probability: ███%.
Recommendation: expenditure denied.
Status amended: DECEASED.
// RECORD ENDS //
+=+=+=+=+=[ ◈ ]=+=+=+=+=+
// ATTACHMENT III //
MEDICAL PROCUREMENT AUTHORISATION: Dr KRAIL, Severin
Source: Medical expenditure and casualty review
Following the death of Thermal Systems Technician Ethmet Griz, Foreman Voss ordered review of C-9's reliance on external medical providers. Subsequent assessment identified unacceptable emergency treatment charges and administrative complications arising from repeated use of outside facilities.
Dr. Severin Krail, an independent chirurgeon serving deep-work populations, accepted permanent attachment to GPD C-9. Krail was provided quarters, equipment and a regular retainer in exchange for on-site treatment of Detail personnel. External medical expenditure declined by 83% during the following quarter.  
:: COMPLIANCE NOTE ::
Krail submits mandatory mutation reports within recognised deep-work tolerances. Cases requiring secondary review routinely arrive incomplete or corrupted.
No common filing fault has been identified.

engagements.report:
HOSTILE ENGAGEMENT #2.2 
x PALANITE PRECINCT “FANGS OF JUSTICE”
[■] ADMINISTRATUM INCIDENT RECORD
SUBJECT: Unauthorized Seizure of Promethium Cache 17-Gamma
INVOLVED: Palanite Enforcer Precinct  / Unregistered Menial Laborers
STATUS: PRECINCT ROUTED / TERRITORY LOST
SOURCE: Servitor Surveillance Unit 9-GAMMA-117
**+++ BEGIN TRANSCRIPTION +++**
At 19:43:11, unidentified hostile personnel entered Promethium Cache 17-Gamma. Palanite personnel engaged immediately.
At 19:44:32, two hostile combatants emerged from concealed positions and discharged incendiary weapons at close range. Palanite formation disrupted. Additional hostile personnel advanced under cover of the flames.
At 19:46:18, hostile commander identified as **JAREK VOSS**, designation *“Foreman”*, engaged Palanite melee specialist **IRON SHROUD**. Engagement lasted 41.7 seconds. IRON SHROUD incapacitated Jarek Voss. Palanite tactical assessment indicated local superiority. Assessment incorrect.
At 19:47:06, hostile individual **GARRICK VOSS** discharged a krak grenade at point-blank range. Projectile impacted IRON SHROUD with catastrophic result. Remaining Palanite personnel subsequently trampled the incapacitated hostile commander during the engagement. On the eastern flank, three hostile incendiary weapons and multiple lasguns inflicted sustained casualties. Palanite formation collapsed.
At 19:49:51, sanctioned psychic personnel initiated an unidentified psychic manifestation. Hostile response: negligible. No loss of cohesion was observed.
NOTE: No approved classification exists for the observed phenomenon. Pursuant to Standing Directive XEN-17/Theta - “Ignorance is no exemption from vigilance” - immediate referral to Ordo Xenos is mandatory.
At 19:51:07, Palanite resistance ceased to constitute organized military action. Withdrawal commenced.
At 19:53:04, all surviving Palanite personnel had exited the engagement area. Hostile personnel remained in possession of the facility.
At 19:54:37, JAREK VOSS was observed standing and resuming command activity despite having been incapacitated approximately eight minutes prior.  
:: ANALYSIS ::
The engagement cannot be classified as a successful Palanite enforcement action. Hostile force demonstrated effective ambush tactics, coordinated incendiary deployment, resistance to psychic disruption and extreme command resilience.
Palanite casualties: **[DATA EXPUNGED]**
  

+ TERRITORIAL CONTROL: HOSTILE
Promethium Cache 17-Gamma is assessed as compromised.
+ RECOMMENDATION: Reclassify hostile organization as **confirmed ██████████████ ███████ presence**. 
[ERR::XEN-09 // KILL-ORDER ISSUED] 
+ SECONDARY RECOMMENDATION: DO NOT ATTEMPT immediate recovery with equivalent force strength.
// INCIDENT CLOSED :: POST-ENGAGEMENT PROCESSING //
engagements.addenda:

// ATTACHMENT I //
PERSONNEL REASSIGNMENT: ROOK, Veyl “V-ROOK”
Source: Post-engagement security review
Following acquisition of Promethium Cache 17-Gamma, Foreman Voss requested permanent reassignment of Penal Labour Asset Veyl Rook from auxiliary survey duties to armed perimeter observation. Review of the preceding engagement identified repeated exposure of advancing work parties to hostile personnel beyond effective response range.

// RECORD ENDS //
+=+=+=+=+=[ ◈ ]=+=+=+=+=+
// ATTACHMENT II //
COMMERCIAL ARRANGEMENT: VEYNE, Marcella
Source: Peregrine's Due commercial correspondence
Voss,
Your people keep finding things they aren't paid to find.
I have buyers for some of them. For the rest, I have people who know what they're looking at. Anything recovered from the lower workings that isn't obviously Imperial comes to me first. In return, I'll make available suitable off-world equipment, restricted salvage and documentation sufficient to explain why C-9 possesses either.
My cargo can use your lower routes where necessary. Your manifests remain yours. Mine remain mine. Neither of us becomes curious about the difference.
Anything C-9 wishes moved off-world can travel under the same arrangement, provided it is sealed before my people collect it. I do not inspect clients' cargo unless they give me reason to.
This arrangement does not extend to personnel.
— M. Veyne
 Peregrine's Due  
:: HANDWRITTEN ANNOTATION ::
Garrick—
Give her whatever we recover that we cannot use. Take anything useful she brings back.
For outbound consignments, use sealed containers only. No markings. No explanation. Do not tell her what she's carrying.
She thinks we're using her ship to move contraband.
We are.
—Voss
// RECORD ENDS //
+=+=+=+=+=[ ◈ ]=+=+=+=+=+
// ATTACHMENT III //
SITE INTEGRATION: PROMETHIUM CACHE 17-GAMMA
Source: C-9 internal shift communications following cessation of hostilities
GARRICK: Cache is secure. Main reservoir looks intact. Mara says the transfer system can be brought back online before the next shift.
VOSS: Good. Have her do it. We can run the forward generators from here instead of hauling fuel through the Toll Crossing.
GARRICK: Jarek, there's something else. The precinct markings on the equipment are the same as the Toll Crossing.
[6.34s pause registered]
VOSS: I know.
GARRICK: Same precinct, then. Twice.
VOSS: Twice that we know of.
GARRICK: First we take their crossing. Now we take their promethium. At some point they're going to stop thinking we're miners who happen to be armed.
VOSS: They don't need to think we're miners. They need to think we're miners who steal, smuggle and shoot Enforcers when cornered. There are thousands of those.
GARRICK: And if they start asking why we're so good at it?
[Routine traffic omitted: pressure readings, storage counts.] 
VOSS: Then we have been too memorable.
GARRICK: Give the Cache back?
VOSS: No. That would be memorable too. Strip their markings, put the tanks back into service and file it as abandoned industrial salvage. We keep the Cache. We stop picking fights with the Fangs.
GARRICK: Think they'll agree?
VOSS: No.
SITE STATUS :: PROMETHIUM CACHE 17-GAMMA — OPERATIONAL
CONTROL :: GEOTHERMAL PROSPECT DETAIL C-9
ADMINISTRATIVE DESIGNATION :: RECOVERED INDUSTRIAL INFRASTRUCTURE
// RECORD ENDS //
+=+=+=+=+=[ ◈ ]=+=+=+=+=+
// ATTACHMENT IV //
ADDENDUM: THE IRON SHROUD
Source: Transcribed canteen audio-log, Labour Rest Station ██-17
Speakers: Unidentified contract labourers
Archive classification: WORKER FOLKLORE / NON-ACTIONABLE 
“You hear things working the lower levels. This one came from a pipe-fitter who'd done a few shifts alongside C-9. Said their children are told not to wander beyond the work lamps after shift-change. Sensible enough. The old tunnels have bad air, loose stone and things that belong to other people.
And then there is the Iron Shroud.
They say Vandrus of the Fangs of Justice was a man once, before the hive started taking pieces of him. It took his face first and left the scars, then reached inside his skull. Something else went after that, though nobody agrees what. Every time he comes back there's another plate, another scar, another part that hurts when he walks. That's why the C-9 children are warned not to laugh if they see him.
Jarek Voss did, apparently. Or maybe he spat at him. Or called him something. That's the trouble with stories from C-9: everybody remembers the same ending and a different beginning. Some say Voss emptied all three pistols into the Shroud. The pipe-fitter reckoned it was only two. Doesn't matter. Vandrus kept coming and put the Foreman down.
Garrick saw his brother fall and fired a krak grenade into the Shroud at point-blank range. Vandrus went down too.
Both men survived. That's the part the children like.
The older ones say the Iron Shroud can't die because there's too little of the original man left for Death to recognise. The younger ones say he collects injuries from people who run from him, and the scars under his armour are waiting to find their way onto somebody else.
Supposedly Voss heard the stories and told C-9 to stop talking about the Iron Shroud. The pipe-fitter swore they did. Never heard another word about Vandrus from any of them.
Funny thing was, they all still knew the story. Same details. Same warnings to the children. Even the ones who hadn't been there.
Asked one of them once who told him.
He looked at me like it was a stupid question.”
// RECORD ENDS //
:: ENGAGEMENT DOSSIER CLOSED :: All attached records entered into the sector archive. Outstanding discrepancies deemed non-material. Further review neither required nor authorised. // FILE SEALED // THE EMPEROR PROTECTS

engagements.report:
HOSTILE ENGAGEMENT #3.1
x HELMAETH EXPEDITIONARY FORCE
[■] FORMAL CLAIM OF INTERFERENCE
ORIGIN: Helmaeth Expeditionary Force
FILED WITH: Hive Primus Guild Office / Office of Territorial Arbitration
SUBJECT: Collapse Freight Exchange 17-KAPPA / disputed salvage rights
REQUESTED REMEDY: Compensation, recognition of prior claim, commencement of parley
The Helmaeth Expeditionary Force submits that Geothermal Prospect Detail C-9 unlawfully removed a Mechanicus-pattern technical servitor from Collapse Freight Exchange 17-KAPPA (commonly referred to as: The Old Ruins) while ownership of recoverable material within said site remained under dispute. Helmaeth personnel attempted to intercept the machine prior to its removal. C-9 responded with armed force.
This was not, as subsequently claimed, a routine movement of industrial equipment. Two restricted C-9 labour assets were already concealed along the western approach when Helmaeth personnel arrived. Both employed incendiary weapons, causing casualties and sufficient disruption for additional C-9 personnel to enter the sector. Although both assets were eventually incapacitated, a further worker continued the attack using incendiary charges.
The servitor meanwhile advanced through the central workings under escort by Foreman Jarek Voss and armed personnel associated with the Peregrine's Due. Helmaeth Charter Master Thrain engaged the escort after a seismic grenade struck the group at close concentration. Despite multiple personnel being thrown from position, the advance continued. Thrain subsequently entered close contact and was himself incapacitated. Witnesses identify C-9 worker Hask Drenn as responsible for the final blow.
Attempts to contain the remaining approaches were unsuccessful. A C-9 survey engineer and accompanying worker prevented reinforcement from the eastern sector, while a marksman positioned above the central route continued observation despite being struck and falling from his position. The marksman was subsequently observed climbing back to the same position.
By cessation of hostilities, the western C-9 element had been neutralised and multiple members of the escort had sustained injuries. The technical servitor remained operational, however, and the route to the extraction boundary had been cleared. Continued interception was assessed as commercially unjustifiable.
Helmaeth Expeditionary Force therefore contests C-9's subsequent registration of the Old Ruins and requests compensation for lost salvage rights, medical expenditure, damaged equipment and interruption of legitimate prospecting operations.  


:: ATTACHED RESPONSE, GPD C-9 ::
Foreman Voss has agreed to parley. No admission of liability has been entered.


:: ADMINISTRATUM REVIEW ::  
Claimant acknowledges initiating armed interception of registered labour personnel transporting industrial equipment.
No prior Helmaeth title to the disputed servitor has been produced.
Registered asset: COLLAPSED FREIGHT EXCHANGE 17-KAPPA
Registered controller: GEOTHERMAL PROSPECT DETAIL C-9
Request for compulsory restitution: DENIED
Request for voluntary commercial arbitration: PERMITTED 
// INCIDENT CLOSED :: POST-ENGAGEMENT PROCESSING //

Following denial of compulsory restitution, representatives of the Helmaeth Expeditionary Force requested parley with Foreman Jarek Voss concerning salvage rights, medical costs and loss of access to the disputed site.
Helmaeth submitted claims against the recovered technical servitor, associated salvage and projected revenues from the Exchange. Voss rejected ownership of the servitor as grounds for territorial claim, but accepted Helmaeth's valuation of the site for purposes of calculating compensation for C-9 personnel injured while establishing control of it.
Following revision, Helmaeth withdrew all claims against the servitor and recognised C-9 control of Exchange 17-Kappa. C-9 withdrew its counterclaim for injury, obstruction and recovery costs.

// RECORD ENDS //
+=+=+=+=+=[ ◈ ]=+=+=+=+=+
// ATTACHMENT III //
SURGICAL RECORD: LABOUR ASSET K-117
Source: Dr. Severin Krail, operative audio-log
Procedure: Emergency trauma surgery / lower limb reconstruction
Patient presents with extensive trauma to the left leg. Projectile entered below the knee and... no. That's not right. There's a second articulation beneath the muscle. I'm going to extend the incision.
[pause]
Right. That's deliberate anatomy. Not a tumour, not a fused joint. The vascular structure feeds it normally. Bone growth is mature and symmetrical. I've seen deep-work mutations before. This isn't one. 
[recording resumes 38 minutes later]
Bleeding controlled. Primary joint is salvageable, secondary structure less so. I've fixed what I understand and left alone what I don't. Patient should walk, though there will be permanent loss of mobility.
I should take a sample.
[11.2s pause]
I should report this.
Lasting impairment: HOBBLED
Samples submitted: NONE
// RECORD ENDS //
+=+=+=+=+=[ ◈ ]=+=+=+=+=+
// ATTACHMENT IV //
INTERCEPTED SHORE CORRESPONDENCE
Source: Peregrine's Due encrypted vox traffic
Participants: Harlon Rusk / Garrick Voss
Subject: Imperial inquiry concerning Jarek Voss
RUSK: We've got a problem. The Exchange incident reached people who are asking about your brother. Captain wants him out of sight until it dies down.
GARRICK: He does not agree.
RUSK: I've only just told you.
GARRICK: He knows.
[6.8s pause]
RUSK: Fine. His name is tied to Veyne's charter, our manifests and inquiries I'd rather not reopen. If they find him, they'll start asking what passes between C-9 and the Peregrine's Due.
GARRICK: Can you stop it?
RUSK: Probably. Hiding your Foreman would be cheaper.
GARRICK: He won't disappear. He's at the parley.
[4.2s pause]
RUSK: Of course he is. I'm trying to convince the Imperium nobody can find him while he's sitting in a Guild office.
GARRICK: We need the agreement.
RUSK: And I need you people to understand the concept of lying low.
GARRICK: He knows.
[9.5s pause]
RUSK: I'm starting to dislike that word.
GARRICK: Can you stop the inquiry?
RUSK: Probably. Captain considers it a favour.
GARRICK: He knows.
RUSK: Stop that.
:: ALLIANCE STATUS :: DISQUIET
:: COMMERCIAL ARRANGEMENT :: MAINTAINED

engagements.report:
HOSTILE ENGAGEMENT #3.2
x HOUSE ORLOCK GANG “THE SLAG EATERS”
[■] INTERCEPTED SLAG EATERS JOB RECORD
Job: Sludge Sea claim
Opposition: Geothermal Prospect Detail C-9
Result: PULLED OUT
Claim: FAILED


Looked easy.
Some mining crew had settled around the Sea and put up enough guns to call it theirs. We came in fast, took two marks before they properly got moving and left them boxed around the last one.  
C-9 didn't try taking either back. They shut themselves in around the third.
After that we weren't chasing miners out of a claim. We had to go through them.
We tried the sides first. Found more of them waiting where nobody had seen them go. Tried the other way and got much the same, except with considerably more fire. They didn't hold ground like road crews and they didn't come running when we took theirs. They waited until we'd committed and then started closing the ways back out.  
Then we started getting a proper look at them.
Some could pass for miners. Some couldn't. Extra arms under work coats. Heads the wrong shape. One big bastard built like something dredged out of a sump. They had military hardware mixed in with the work gear and enough incendiaries to turn the passages into furnaces. There were off-worlders fighting beside them too—Veyne's lot, unless somebody else is running around with a Kroot and an Ork these days.
Still could've been mutants with good connections.
Then the shots started missing.
Not bad shots. Good ones. Clear ones.
One of the little things following their Foreman would twitch and he'd move before the trigger broke. Saw the same thing happen more than once. Men ducking shots they couldn't see coming. Turning toward trouble before it came around the corner.
Not fast. Early. Don't know what that is.  
We got through their front eventually. Put one of Veyne's xenos down and shook their Foreman badly enough that he disappeared back into the workings. For about half a minute it looked like we'd cracked them.
The miners kept fighting.
One side came back burned. The other came back bloodied. Gregg somehow came back from his side still standing, which is more than can be said for most of what went in with him. Then something started shooting out of the doorway we'd spent the whole job trying to get through. Ash went down hard. One of those little four-legged things crawling around their boots finished a kid on the floor.
That changed the arithmetic.
We still had guns. We still had men. What we didn't have was a clean road to the last mark. Both ways around had failed, the way through was starting to run in the wrong direction, and the miners still had another position behind all of it.  
There isn't enough money in a Sludge Sea to keep feeding people into that.
Eisen pulled us out.  
:: NOTES FOR Y’ALL ::
C-9 aren't a mining crew with guns. Don't know what they are yet.
They burn easily enough. They bleed. They get scared. Just don't count on any of that stopping the others.
And if one of those little things is looking at you, assume somebody else already knows where you are.
Sludge Sea: THEIR PROBLEM  


RECOVERED WORKSITE AUDIO
Source: C-9 shift-channel buffer
Recording status: Incidental
MARA: I know, same thing happened to me when Rusk and the Ork went down.
JAREK: Couldn't feel anyone?
MARA: Barely. Like everyone went far away.
JAREK: I couldn't hear anything. When the hammer took the Kroot down, there was just him, then the hammer, then me.
JAREK: Is that what fear is like for everyone else?
[8.3s silence]
MARA: Throne…




// INCIDENT CLOSED :: POST-ENGAGEMENT PROCESSING //

// ATTACHMENT I //

// ATTACHMENT II //
TERMINATION OF COMMERCIAL ARRANGEMENT
Source: Peregrine's Due commercial correspondence
Sender: Marcella Veyne
Recipient: Jarek Voss


Voss,
I put my people beside yours because the arrangement was profitable. Since then I have altered manifests, buried inquiries, moved cargo I was specifically paid not to inspect and spent favors keeping your business separate from mine. When Imperial attention finally settled on you personally, I asked you to disappear for a few days. You refused.
I tolerated that because C-9 remained useful. Then you took my Shore Party into a Sludge Sea. Grubnak was carried out. Rusk spent most of the engagement bleeding on the floor. Kharakh broke through the Orlock line for you and received an arc hammer for his trouble.
I asked Rusk what C-9 was protecting. He didn't know.
I asked whether you had told any of them why that patch of poisoned water was worth their lives. You hadn't.
I don't require honesty from my business partners, Voss. I do require enough information to decide what I am risking my people for.
Effective immediately, the Peregrine's Due will no longer carry C-9 consignments. Cold Trade inventory is closed to you. The Shore Party will not answer further requests from the Detail.
Anything already aboard my ship will reach its destination. I keep my contracts even when other people make them difficult.
Do not approach the Peregrine's Due. Do not use my routes. Do not send Garrick to explain.
If I decide there is still business between us, I will find you.
— M. Veyne
